_meta.note: Add a DISCOVERY MODE to the code adapter: a pure function over a codemap ({edges:[[A,B]]}, A depends on B) that, given entry-point symbols + a direction, returns the transitively-reachable affected symbols + the induced subgraph. Directions: `dependents` (reverse reachability = change-impact: who depends on the entry), `dependencies` (forward: what it needs), `both`. This is Seam 1 used FORWARD (discover scope before authoring the DAG) instead of only validating a written DAG — the affected set is then mapped (by human/LLM judgment) to tasks, and deplint checks the ordering. It is a NEW shared surface => a PARITY surface (node `codegraph-discover.js` + python `codegraph_discover.py`, byte-equal deterministic sorted output) with its own parity case, and an MCP tool `code_discover` so an MCP client (Codex/Claude Code/OpenCode) gets it host-neutral. Stays ADVISORY (report, never rewrite the DAG); docs stay honest that the graph models resolved static edges, NOT dynamic/framework bindings (Alpine methods, templates) or not-yet-existing symbols. Built proof-driven: spec-first proofs, both runtimes at parity, gated + refuted; suites (node/python/parity/prose/self-audit) stay green.

phases.title: Discovery core — pure reachability, both runtimes, gated + parity

tasks.title: Spec-first: author the discovery proofs + fixture (before any impl)
tasks.description: Write the gated proofs BEFORE the implementation (they must go RED first). (a) plugin/adapters/code/fixtures/discover-codemap.json: a small codemap {edges:[[A,B]]} exercising a chain, a branch, an unrelated pair, and a cycle — e.g. edges main->service, service->repo, repo->db, api->service, service->auth, util->helper, and a<->b (cycle). (b) docs/howto/gate-examples/code-discover.sh (prints CODE-DISCOVER-OK): runs `node plugin/adapters/code/codegraph-discover.js <fixture> <entry> --dependents|--dependencies|--both` and asserts, from the fixture, that `--dependents repo` = {main,service,api,repo} (transitive callers — change impact) and EXCLUDES db/auth/util/helper; `--dependencies repo` = {repo,db} and excludes main/api; `--both repo` = the union; the entry itself is always included; a cycle entry (a) terminates and yields {a,b}; and the emitted `edges` are the induced subgraph among affected (both endpoints in affected). Compute expected sets in the proof independently of the implementation (enumerate them literally), so the proof is a true oracle. (c) docs/howto/gate-examples/code-discover-parity.sh (prints CODE-DISCOVER-PARITY-OK): runs node and `python3 -m heartbeat.adapters.code.codegraph_discover` on the fixture for EACH direction and asserts byte-identical stdout. Both proofs must FAIL now (no codegraph-discover.js yet) — confirm red.

tasks.title: Implement the node discovery provider
tasks.description: Write plugin/adapters/code/codegraph-discover.js: a PURE function discover(codemap, entries, direction) over codemap.edges ([[A,B]] = A depends on B). `dependents` = transitive reverse-reachability (all X with X ->* entry — change impact); `dependencies` = transitive forward-reachability (all Y with entry ->* Y); `both` = union. BFS/DFS with a visited set (cycle-safe, terminates). Always include the entries in `affected`. Output DETERMINISTIC JSON with SORTED arrays: {"entry":[...sorted],"direction":"...","affected":[...sorted],"edges":[[...]] sorted} where `edges` is the induced subgraph (both endpoints in affected). CLI: `node codegraph-discover.js <codemap.json> <e1,e2,...> [--dependents|--dependencies|--both]` (default --both); imports nothing from core. Make code-discover.sh (node assertions) pass.

tasks.title: Implement the python twin (parity)
tasks.description: Write py/src/heartbeat/adapters/code/codegraph_discover.py mirroring the node provider exactly — same reachability semantics, same sorted deterministic output, same CLI (`python3 -m heartbeat.adapters.code.codegraph_discover <codemap.json> <entries> [--flag]`). Match node's JSON serialization so stdout is BYTE-identical (separators, key order, sorting). Add py/tests/test_adapters_code.py cases for discover (dependents/dependencies/both, cycle, entry-included). Make code-discover-parity.sh (node == python) pass and keep tests/parity.sh green.

tasks.title: Wire the proofs into the suite
tasks.description: Add a new group T98 to tests/run-tests.sh that RUNS code-discover.sh and code-discover-parity.sh and greps their markers on the same check line (CODE-DISCOVER-OK / CODE-DISCOVER-PARITY-OK) — not a bare filename mention. Confirm the node suite is green (RESULT: N passed, 0 failed) with T98 in GROUPS-PASSED, python pytest green, and tests/parity.sh green.

GATE_DC.desc: Discovery is a pure, cycle-safe, deterministic reachability function correct in all three directions (dependents=change-impact, dependencies, both), shipped in BOTH runtimes byte-equal (a parity surface), and wired into the suite.

review.prompt: Refute that DC is done. Does `dependents` compute REVERSE reachability (transitive callers = change impact) and not accidentally forward? Does `dependencies` compute forward? Is the entry always included; do CYCLES terminate (visited set) rather than loop; are unrelated symbols excluded? Is the output truly DETERMINISTIC (sorted affected AND edges) so the parity byte-equality is real, not luck — and is node ACTUALLY byte-identical to python (not both wrong the same way)? Do code-discover.sh / code-discover-parity.sh have TEETH (would they go red if the direction were flipped or a symbol leaked)? Is the fixture-proof oracle independent of the implementation (expected sets enumerated literally, not read back from the code)? Are node/python/parity suites green with T98 wired (marker asserted on the same line, not a bare filename)?
